fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chronos, Kairos and the Real Self", "body": "Chance spent a long stretch on the tower as a tool for questioning the self. He described Kant's idea that the self was neither appearance nor thing in itself but a third status tied to time, and he separated chronos, the measured time of the zodiac and the sun, from kairos, the subjective time in which a soul changes. Chance said many people lived as slaves to chronos by repeating the same routine, while kairos was the movement of the real self. He added that expecting others to change or not to change was a choice, and tied it to biofield tuning."}, {"title": "The Tower Card, Pe and the Mouth", "body": "Chance named the tower as the theme card of the finale and said its Hebrew letter Pe meant mouth and carried the value 80. He said words he counted as 80, including one for a covering multitude and one for a heap or ruin, fit the overlapping voices of the opening montage and the ruined citadel. Gabe said he had long linked the tower to the constellation Pegasus and later tied it to the clock tower constellation Horologium. Gabe also said necromancy was originally ventriloquism and compared the seance of science to throwing a voice."}, {"title": "Hod, Netzach and the Tower Path", "body": "Chance placed the tower card on the Kabbalah tree of life path between Hod and Netzach and read the two Lokis through it. He described Hod as glory and linked it to Loki, whom he called an Enneagram individualist, and Netzach as endurance and victory and linked it to Sylvie. Chance also said the dove on the tower card stood for passive love and matched Loki, while the serpent stood for active love and matched Sylvie. He added that each of them seemed to see the other's path reflected in a mirror."}, {"title": "Rennes-le-Chateau and the Asmodeus Statue", "body": "Gabe said the castle on the skyline reminded him of Rennes-le-Chateau, pointing to a greenhouse beside the tower in the series and at the real castle. He and Chance matched the color of the blanket from the previous episode to the robe on the Asmodeus statue there. Chance said, citing George Faber, that king of the demons referred to Hermes as guide of the spirits of the dead, not to Satan ruling hell. Chance also passed along a find from Jen about a devil standing on an egg in the French cathedral shown in episode one."}, {"title": "Memory Palaces and the Offer They Already Had", "body": "Gabe said the hosts were building memory palaces, with the zodiac as his own, and that the work was remembering rather than learning. Chance said preparing the slides deepened what he already knew, and the long first half led the hosts to split the finale into two parts. The hosts read Miss Minutes' offer to the two Lokis as a temptation to gain something they already held, and Chance compared it to the temptation of Jesus and said the Ion Chronos statues suggested the tempter was inner. Later Chance brought up kintsugi as a picture of being more beautiful for having been broken."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: For the climactic conclusion of our analysis of Loki, Season 1, we explore the pathways of the Kabbalistic Tree of Life, the deepest esoteric understandings of The Tower card of the Major Arcana, the spheres of Hod and Netzach, the letter Pey, the mysteries of Kronos/Saturn, and much more. Who is the man behind the curtain, and where can we find the End of Time? Join us as we deep dive into this episode, For All Time, Always.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "I'm just now wrapping my head around how the word for necromancy, like controlling the dead, is ventriloquism. And that's what we do when we do the seance of science. We summon Einstein into the conversation. We evoke his magical formula, E equals mc squared.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "But anyway, the other word the Greeks have for time is kairos.
